tables.label: Table 1
tables.caption: Minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of peptides and antibiotics against clinical and drug-resistant staphylococci isolates.
footnotes: a(MSSA): methicillin sensitive Staphylococcus aureus; (MRSA): methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus; (VISA): vancomycin intermediate Staphylococcus aureus and (MRSE): methicillin resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis.

tables.label: Table 2
tables.caption: Minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of peptides and antibiotics against clinical vancomycin resistant Staphylococcus aureus (VRSA) isolates.

tables.label: Table 3
tables.caption: The fractional inhibitory concentration index range of peptides in combination with each other and with antibiotics against Staphylococcus aureus isolates.
footnotes: a∑FICI, fractional inhibitory concentration index. FIC index was interpreted as follows: An FIC index of ≤0.5 is considered to demonstrate synergy. Additive was defined as an FIC index of 1. Antagonism was defined as an FIC index of >4. nd, not determined. (MSSA): methicillin sensitive Staphylococcus aureus; (MRSA): methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus; (VRSA): vancomycin resistant Staphylococcus aureus and (MRSE) methicillin resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis.

tables.label: Table 4
tables.caption: Resensitization of vancomycin resistant S. aureus (VRSA) to vancomycin, teicoplanin and oxacillin using a sub-inhibitory concentration (½ × MIC) of WR12 or D-IK8.
footnotes: aFold of re-sensitization: it is the ratio of the MIC of antibiotic alone divided by the MIC of antibiotic after re-sensitization with (½ × MIC) of peptides (WR12 or D-IK8).
